why: f(n) is 2^L - 1 where L is n's bit length, so the candidates are all numbers with at most L bits. Those with exactly k set bits (k = popcount(n)) number C(L, k): choose which k of the L positions are 1. Subtract 1 for n itself.
hints: First work out f(n): the smallest all-ones number >= n has the same bit length L as n.
Every x in [1, 2^L - 1] is an L-bit pattern (with leading zeros allowed); having k ones is choosing k positions out of L.
pitfalls: Exclude n itself (the -1); if n is all ones the answer is 0.
Do not loop up to f(n); n can be near 2^31.
x must be positive, but since k >= 1 the zero pattern is never counted anyway.
